Now has over 200 curated battles.

notes.title: Version 0.92
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] Added new game mode Curated Battles, basically a bunch of set piece battles or generated skirmish battles. You can and should save whatever you like from them to use in your own skirmish battles.

[*] Added a bunch of changes to hopefully make the game more new player friendly. Such as locks in the calibration campaign, so players have to beat easier difficulty levels before advancing. And a recommend unit button for the arcade mode, that will create a unit and shot for you to beat the stage. The recommended unit is very basic but should get you through the arcade, you are of course encouraged to customize the unit to your heart’s content should you feel like it.

[/list]

notes.title: Version 0.9
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] Added Mage spectator, now whenever you died or press the possess key, you possess a mage spectator from which you can either watch the battle or possess another one of your teams units.
[*] Added Player Auto Aim. While not recommended, its preferable to stack health in your favor, it allows you to fire at targets using the same method the AI uses. Useful if your fighting against harder AI’s without using the laser shot.
[*] Added more Animations. Anything with a 2D at the end means it only has animations for a 2D plane, namely forward back and left and right. The character with a 2D animation will not react changes in height. Whereas a 3D animation changes the position of the legs when going up or down.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 0.8 and out of early access
notes.notes:
Added Arcade settings, much like the campaign settings allows you to customize your campaign, arcade settings allow you to customize your arcade play through.
You can pick which maps you’ll fight on.
What type of weather.
How much higher or lower of a power level you’ll have in comparison to the AI.
Whether you can see the AI team’s setup before the battle.
The AI type and difficulty.
The number of different unit types.
The minimum and maximum speed of the AI team.
How much the power level of each arcade stage increases by.
The starting power level of the arcade.
And the maximum power level of the arcade.

Why Magocracy Experimentation is no longer in early access.

When I made the early access page last year I didn’t realize how far I would get by this time. If you remember the early access description, my future plans for development were basically finishing up the arcade mode. Which is now done with the release of Version 0.8.

notes.title: Version 0.507

Fixed arcade not loading correct previous arcade game state when losing, caused by loading the previous skirmish game instead of the previous arcade game. Changed laser material for large radius laser to Tron outline.

notes.title: Version 0.504
notes.notes:
Added the ability to pick custom meshes for the campaign, in the campaign settings menu. No longer will you be forced to see a red mannequin fight a blue mannequin. Now see what glorious creations RNG can give you! Or make your characters in the character creation and use those instead.

Added the ability to pick the color of the shots for both the player and the AI teams in the campaign settings menu.

notes.title: Version 0.503
notes.notes:
Biggest changes:
Added a 3d radar to the upper left of the player screen. The radar extends to 10x the unit speed and tracks friendly and enemy positions.
Added a selected target direction to the upper middle of the screen. This only shows up if the target is not on screen. It should help players keep track of the target during high speed fights.

Minor changes:
For large projectiles changed from a shaded transparent material to a Tron like material where the edges are emitters but the center is clear. Hopefully will help players see the target better when using projectiles larger than 1 m radius.

notes.title: Demo Released!
notes.notes:
The Demo for Magocracy: Experimentation has been released!

Here’s what it includes:
3 of the 10 campaigns:
Calibration campaign where you will learn what campaign settings you will use throughout the rest of the campaigns such as unit speed.
Normal Shot campaign where you will learn about all the important variables in a normal shot and how they affect shooting.
Unit campaign where you will learn about all the important variables in a unit and how they affect flying and the AI.

Skirmish: where you can create your own battles choosing what units to deploy, armed with whatever shot values you desire. 

Character Customization: where you can customize your character for Skirmish.
